entries.description: Every customer PHP version gets the OPcache isolation drop-in in its FPM conf.d: no customer script reads another's cached files or drives the shared cache. The drop-in is ours alone, so the copy is the state.

Every customer gets an own PHP-FPM master per version they use, hestia-php<ver>-fpm@<user>; their pools move out of the shared version master, suspended customers' included. Before web-isolation-rebuild, so that rebuild already writes into the new layout and nothing moves twice.

Web domains rendered again: apache binds every fcgi handler a .htaccess sets to the domain's own pool, and the pools lose /tmp. A PHP profile under /etc/hestia/templates takes the new one only while it is as 0.40 shipped it, an edited one is named.

A .php that no domain vhost claims goes to a socket nobody listens on instead of a server-wide Require all denied, so the vhosts no longer grant again in Files context and a customer's .htaccess Require (basic auth, Require ip) protects .php as it protects every other file. Takes effect with the vhost rebuild of this release

apache runs no CGI any more: mod_fcgid ran every executable .fcgi in a docroot as www-data, past the customer boundary, and /cgi-bin/ served its scripts as plain text. mod_fcgid, mod_suexec and mod_actions are switched off, libapache2-mod-fcgid and apache2-suexec-custom purged; existing cgi-bin directories stay as they are, outside every docroot
